title: POLICY & PROCEDURE FOR USE OF NARCOTIC DRUGS AND PSYCHOTROPIC SUBSTANCES
html:
POLICY & PROCEDURE

FOR USE OF NARCOTIC DRUGS AND PSYCHOTROPIC SUBSTANCES

  • PURPOSE:

To ensure safe and rational use of Narcotic and Psychotropic substances

  • SCOPE:
    • Pharmacy
    • Hospital Wide – All Inpatient care areas
  • RESPONSIBILTY:
    • Medical Director
    • Administrator
    • Consultants / Doctors
    • Nursing Staff
    • Pharmacy and Therapeutic Committee
  • ABBREVIATION:
    • ICU: Intensive Care Unit
    • MOM: Management Of Medication
    • NABH: National Accreditation Board For Hospitals and Healthcare providers
    • NDPS: Narcotic Drugs & Psychotropic Substances
    • RMO: Resident Medical Officer
  • DEFINITION:

Nil

  • REFERENCE:

NABH Standards for Hospitals

  • POLICY:
    • Hospital does not have a NDPS license; so our pharmacy does not deal with such drugs.
    • The policy is to order the needed narcotic & psychotropic drugs from the pharmacy which has an authorized NDPS license against patient specific prescription by medical practitioner.
    • Usage of narcotics drugs and psychotropic substances are in consonance with Narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances act.
    • A proper record of its uses, administration and disposal is maintained.
    • Only appropriate personnel handle these drugs in accordance with policies.
    • Issues done under perpetual declining inventory and against prescription from the medical practitioner. The prescribing practitioner is responsible in case the prescription does not conform to statutory regulations.
    • Nursing station ensures the entry of drug in register while administering.
    • Security clause for storage:
      • All containers used for holding and storing narcotic drugs are properly labelled. Appropriate registers are maintained to have enough information on its usage.
      • Drugs when indented are kept under the charge of the nurse. All narcotics and controlled drugs are to be kept under double lock and key
      • The Ward in-charge may delegate this responsibility to a senior nurse when she is absent from the ward.
    • New issues of narcotic drugs are checked by the sister on receipt, recorded in the register and immediately locked into the appropriate cupboard.
    • The narcotic drugs register incorporates a record of all receipt and issue involving narcotic drugs.
    • A proper record of its uses, administration and disposal is maintained at all the places wherever narcotic drugs are stored.
    • Stocking of narcotics on the floors is not permitted; only should be indented against a patient.
  • PROCEDURE:
    • Usage & Documentation:
      • The narcotic or similar dangerous drugs are only issued for use after receiving written and signed orders from the treating doctor or the anaesthesiologist by the authorize pharmacy.
      • Psychotropic drugs are also administered under the specific orders from a doctor.
      • The patient is under the care of a nursing staff at least for an hour after administrating the drugs.
      • Nursing station ensures the entry of batch number in the patient file and Narcotic register.
      • The nursing staff documents amount administered and discarded with witness signature in the Narcotic Register.
      • In the event that the portion of a drug of dependence remains unused, the unused portion may be discarded personally by the registered nurse.
      • Both persons must document clearly in the Drug Register the amount of drug given as well as the amount of drug discarded.
      • This includes narcotic infusions, which have been ceased prior to completion of contents.
      • Out of date or unused drugs are returned to the pharmacist.
      • Both persons sign the register.
      • All narcotics and controlled are written down in the doctors order sheet and the patient’s individual request form by the ordering doctor.
      • No narcotics and/or controlled drug can be administered by a nurse without written order by the Consultant/Houseman. A verbal/telephone order can be accepted only under unusual circumstances as per nursing policy, which should be countersigned by the doctors within 2hrs.
      • All narcotics and controlled drug are to be properly recorded by the nurse in the Narcotics and Controlled drug Account book located in each department. This will routinely be done when the drug is being drawn up and prior to the drug being administered to the patient.
      • NO erasures and/or whiteout can be used on Narcotics and Controlled Drug Account Book and pharmacy sheet. The use of line drawn to through the entry and marked “ERROR” can be utilized when necessary. Two nurse signatures shall also be needed on in this particular situation.
      • All narcotics and controlled drug that are administered are properly recorded immediately by the nurse in the medical record and/or the patient’s medication record and the pharmacy sheet.
      • An oncoming and outgoing registered nurse physically count the drugs and the empty ampoules together and sign their names/titles on the Narcotics and Controlled Drug Count Form. Two nurses from the same shift cannot count the Narcotics and Controlled Drugs.
      • Empty ampoules of narcotics and controlled drug should be returned to the pharmacy. Both persons must identify the patient, the drug and witness the administration of the drug. The person administering the drug then signs the medication chart.
    • Storage and accounting of narcotics:
      • All narcotic drugs shall be kept in double lock & key under the supervision of a nominated person.
      • All transaction records shall be maintained for three years.
      • Every order for narcotic drug should contain prescriber name, date, reg. no. along with the name & doses of drug.
      • Patient specific drug administration / consumption record shall be maintained for two years.
      • Information about losses/theft shall be given to local police station and excise inspector.
      • Disposal of Unused Narcotics will be done by nursing in presence of doctor, who will sign the records, mentioning the approximate amount of narcotics disposed.
      • If the registered nurse leave the ward area the keys must be handed to the registered nurse remaining who is then in-charge of the ward.
      • In the event that the drug keys are taken from the hospital every effort must be made to contact the person identified as having the keys for their return as soon as possible.
    • Breakage, loss, theft or expiry of narcotics
      • In the event of loss or breakage of a drug of dependence notify the senior nurse and the pharmacist at the earliest opportunity.
      • Pharmacist informs Excise inspector
      • Excise inspector will observe the expiry / breakage
      • After observing the breakage / expiry records, Excise inspector will destroy them & enter his remark in the record with his signature & date, Qty. of destroyed item.
      • All expired/ breakage stock shall be stored separately with clean & clear label.
      • Theft - If there is any unjustified mismatch in the stock, Excise inspector has to inform a soon as possible.
      • Discrepancy in wards:
        • Any drug discrepancies must be immediately reported to the Departmental I/C Nurse on duty. The pharmacist on duty/on call will be notified by the Nurse In-charge.
        • No nursing staff member can go off duty until the drug discrepancy has been corrected unless approved by the matron.
    • Handling:
      • These drugs are handled by appropriate personnel only.

i.e. Anaesthetist & defined staff in OT

    • Record:
      • These are kept in accordance with statutory requirements.
      • A very strict inventory control shall be kept for these drugs.
      • The empty vials shall be disposed as per local regulatory requirements.
